heroHeadline: India Approves $22B Green Energy Corridor to Transmit 135 GW of Renewables
heroSubtitle: 3,931 days since the Paris Agreement — China's National Energy Administration confirmed (September 1) that installed solar capacity reached 1.286 TW at the end of July 2026, edging past coal's 1.285 TW to end a century of coal dominance in the world's largest power system. The same week, Norway's new-car market hit a world-record 98.7% electric share in August, and the European Commission inaugurated Europe's largest industrial carbon capture facility at Yara's Sluiskil plant in the Netherlands (September 7), capturing up to 800,000 tonnes of CO2 a year for storage under the North Sea. A new UNEP report (September 7) found coordinated climate and clean-air action returns $15 for every $1 invested.
footerNote: Data sourced from IEA, IRENA, Ember, BloombergNEF, Rho Motion, UNFCCC, UNEP, European Commission, and major international outlets. All figures reflect verified, publicly available data through September 2026.
